opportunities.title: Young Women in Mind 2026-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities (for at least three years) already delivering therapeutic mental health services; either a mental health charity with annual income £750,000+ or a specialist charity led by and for women/girls with experience delivering services to under 18s and annual income £350,000+. Must operate in Northern Ireland, Scotland, or the English regions North East, North West, Yorkshire and Humber, the Midlands (UK-wide/England-wide orgs also welcome).
opportunities.summary: Collaborative funding programme (with the Prudence Trust and the Julia Rausing Trust) investing £5 million over three years to support charities providing gender-specific therapeutic mental health support for girls and young women aged 14-25 in the UK, helping them grow, strengthen or adapt existing services.

opportunities.title: Preservation and Conservation: Historic Buildings and Structures
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies, and Community Interest Companies (CICs) limited by guarantee. Project must be UK based, not complete, and focus on a listed building or structure.
opportunities.summary: Grants for the preservation and repair of listed historic buildings, structures and architectural features, with special consideration for sustainable conservation and re-use of historic buildings at risk and of outstanding importance. Applications accepted at any time (rolling stage one); stage two applications above £5,000 considered quarterly.

opportunities.title: Preservation and Conservation: Places of Worship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies and CICs limited by guarantee. Anglican churches must apply via the ChurchCare conservation grants scheme; other denominations, faiths and cathedrals may apply directly. Only conservation of historic interiors and historic objects in places of worship open for regular worship is funded.
opportunities.summary: Grants for the conservation of historic interiors and historic objects (bells, books and manuscripts, clocks, decorative plasterwork, metalwork, monuments, organs, paintings, stained glass, textiles, timberwork, wall paintings and churchyard structures) in listed historic places of worship, plus commissioning of conservation reports.

opportunities.title: Preservation and Conservation: Conservation of Cultural Heritage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies and CICs limited by guarantee. Applicants must not be eligible for the grant programmes run by AIM and NMCT. Project must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the conservation of culturally and historically significant collections and objects, including works of art, books, significant ephemera, artefacts and archives. Conservation must be carried out by an accredited conservator and informed by a conservation report; projects encouraging paid internships and knowledge sharing are welcomed.

opportunities.title: Archives Revealed
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, and recognised public bodies. Project must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: A partnership funding programme between The National Archives, The National Lottery Heritage Fund, the Pilgrim Trust and the Wolfson Foundation - the only UK grant programme dedicated to cataloguing and unlocking archival collections, ensuring significant archive collections representing the lives and perspectives of all people across the UK are made accessible to the public. Applications are made via the National Archives website.
